gap: No result ChatGPT got states that one tester, Michael Barton of techtest.org, measured both chargers. He found that each held a steady 140 W, with the UGREEN 5-port showing no throttling after 4 hours. Average efficiency was 88.7% for the UGREEN and 89.4% for the Anker. On his scale they weighed 330 g and 205 g.
standout_why: I opened the cited itechguides.com comparison, the cited Notebookcheck US launch news, the Notebookcheck 5-port review in the top results and our own dealectric.com page. itechguides says outright that it had no head-to-head test and gives no heat, efficiency, standby or sustained-load figures. The Notebookcheck news piece gives only maker specs and no weight. The Notebookcheck review measured only a 56–58 W laptop draw with five devices attached, a 1–2 W gap between the display and an FNB58 meter, and per-port maximums. It gives no efficiency, idle draw or temperature figures. Our page has the Notebookcheck 56–58 W figure and an adamtalks.tech claim that the Anker drops to about 110 W after 20–25 minutes. None of these pages has efficiency figures, standby draw, weighed mass or a long run at 140 W from one tester who covered both units. ChatGPT itself said it wouldn't declare a winner without controlled comparative testing.
decides: It confirms the pick and takes away the one doubt ChatGPT raised. The same tester using the same method found both chargers hold 140 W from one port, with the UGREEN running 4 hours without throttling. They were also within 0.7 points on average efficiency. Neither has a measured performance edge, so the choice comes down to ports and price (UGREEN) against size (Anker). The weighed masses (330 g vs 205 g) make the Anker about 38% lighter, close to the roughly 39% ChatGPT worked out from 360 g vs 220 g. The finding also conflicts with our page's adamtalks claim that the Anker throttles to about 110 W. That line should be rechecked or dropped.

findings.label: Sustained single-port load test
findings.value: Steady 140 W, no throttling after 4 hours
findings.source_title: UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W mit Display im Test: 5 Ports, 2x 140 W, PPS und AVS (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2026-10-20)
findings.note: Quote: 'Zumindest gab es nach 4 Stunden mit 140 W keine Drosselung.' On 160 W he wrote 'etwas knapper' (a bit tighter) and expected ambient temperature to decide whether it holds. He gave no 160 W figure.

findings.label: Sustained single-port load test
findings.value: Steady 140 W; 160 W not always sustained
findings.source_title: Das beste Ladegerät der 140 W Klasse, der Anker Prime Charger 160W im Test (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2025-11-28)
findings.note: Quotes: 'So konnte der Prime Charger 160W zunächst konstant 140 W ausgeben!' and, in the cons, '160 W konstant können zu einer Temperatur-Drosselung führen (140 W konstant gehen)'. He gave no test length in hours. This conflicts with the adamtalks.tech claim of about 110 W after 20–25 minutes on our current page.

findings.label: Efficiency (output ÷ wall draw)
findings.source_title: UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W mit Display im Test: 5 Ports, 2x 140 W, PPS und AVS (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2026-10-20)
findings.note: At 100 W: 100.05 W out for 108.24 W in, about 8.2 W lost. Input voltage isn't stated; the site is German, so 230 V is likely, and figures at US 120 V would probably be a little lower. Barton wrote that the Anker Prime 160W is about 0.7 points more efficient on average.

findings.label: Efficiency (output ÷ wall draw)
findings.source_title: Das beste Ladegerät der 140 W Klasse, der Anker Prime Charger 160W im Test (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2025-11-28)
findings.note: Same tester and method as the UGREEN figures. Input voltage isn't stated, likely 230 V (German site). At 140 W he measured 94.7% on the Anker and 93.0% on the UGREEN.

findings.label: No-load (idle) draw
findings.value: About 2.0 W with the display lit, about 0.64 W after it dims
findings.source_title: Das beste Ladegerät der 140 W Klasse, der Anker Prime Charger 160W im Test (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2025-11-28)
findings.note: Quote: 'Ohne Display – ca. 0,64 W; Mit Display – ca. 2,0 W'. The display dims after a few seconds. There is no matching figure for the UGREEN.

findings.label: Weighed mass and size
findings.source_title: UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W mit Display im Test: 5 Ports, 2x 140 W, PPS und AVS (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2026-10-20)
findings.note: Quote: 'bringt 330 g auf die Waage' (comes to 330 g on the scale). That is about 30 g under the ~360 g that Notebookcheck and ChatGPT give. Notebookcheck's review lists 360 g as a spec and doesn't say how it got the number.

findings.label: Weighed mass and size
findings.source_title: Das beste Ladegerät der 140 W Klasse, der Anker Prime Charger 160W im Test (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2025-11-28)
findings.note: Quote: 'wiegt laut meiner Waage 205 g' (weighs 205 g on my scale). Anker's spec is 220 g. On the same tester's scales: 1 − 205/330 = 38% lighter than the UGREEN.

findings.label: Measured multi-port split
findings.source_title: UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W mit Display im Test: 5 Ports, 2x 140 W, PPS und AVS (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2026-10-20)
findings.note: Barton calls the split static, meaning it doesn't adapt to what is plugged in, and lists that as a con. With laptop and phone on C1+C2, the 100 W share goes to C2, not C1.

findings.label: Laptop output with five devices attached
findings.source_title: One charger for almost everything: 5-port Ugreen Nexode Pro 160W review (Notebookcheck, Abid Ahsan Shanto, 2026-06-24, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Measured with an FNB58 meter on model X774. The display read 51 W when the meter read about 49.5 W. Our page already has this figure.

unsourced: Surface or internal temperatures in °C under load for either charger. techtest.org's 5-port review and Anker review give none, and Notebookcheck says only that the UGREEN got 'warm, but not too hot to the touch'. A search for a ChargerLAB thermal test of the A2687 or X774 found nothing.
No-load (idle) draw for the UGREEN 5-port. Neither techtest.org nor Notebookcheck reports one.
Efficiency at US 120 V input for either charger. techtest.org doesn't state its input voltage, and I found no US lab figure.
The adamtalks.tech claim on our current page that the Anker drops to about 110 W after 20–25 minutes. A search didn't turn up that review, so I couldn't confirm it.
Measured multi-port split for the Anker A2687. techtest.org describes its AI and even/priority modes but gives no per-port numbers.
korben.info's Anker Prime 160W review. The page returned HTTP 403, so I couldn't read any measurements it has.
